To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stability of PapMV-HA1 nanoparticles is a key factor in the induction of an efficient immune response against the HA11 epitopes.
we have engineered a novel PapMV-HA1 vaccine platform that can be used for the design and development of novel influenza vaccines.
PapMV-HA1 nanoparticles are stable and immunogenic in mice, and that the fusion site has an impact on the nanoparticle stability and the immunogenicity of PapMV-HA 1 nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of PapMV nanoparticles through fusion to several putative surface-exposed sites.
the engineering of PapMV nanoparticles for the delivery of peptide antigens.
the engineering of PapMV nanoparticles for the design of innovative vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fusion of the HA11 peptide to two different sites in PapMV CP led to the production and characterization of stable nanoparticles capable of triggering a strong immune response in animals directed against the HA11 epitopes.
the fusion of the HA11 peptide to the PapMV CP at amino acid position 187 is an excellent way to generate an immunogen that triggers a strong immune response in mice.
the PapMV platform can be used to design and produce a wide range of nanoparticles with different properties, which can be exploited for the development of new vaccines and adjuvants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability and immunogenic potential of PapMV nanoparticles can be modulated by the location of the fusion peptide within the PapMV coat proteins.
the PapMV platform is an efficient vaccine delivery platform that can accommodate several fusion sites and that stability of the nanoparticles is a major determinant of the immunogenicity in vivo.
the PapMV-H187-HA11 fusion is the best candidate to develop a new vaccine against influenza.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PapMV nanoparticles are an efficient platform for the design of innovative vaccines, and the PapMV-H187-HA11 fusion is a good example of the potential of PapMV nanoparticles in the design of innovative flu vaccines.
the PapMV nanoparticle can be engineered through fusion to different sites of the coat protein, and the stability and immunogenic potential of the new nanoparticle can be evaluated.

PapMV is an excellent platform for the development of vaccines and adjuvants, and that the stability of the fusion protein is an important parameter to consider in the development of new PapMV-based vaccines.
